<!-- pr-reviewer: e69163a3eb1f7fc27473a625972a4146f2033c46 -->
**Needs changes before merge** - the scan can be put out of step with ruststep's tokenizer, and a deep record then reaches the parser and still overflows the stack.

### What looks good
- The approach is right: one linear byte pass before ruststep. Memory is bounded and there are no panics. Index math uses `get`/saturating ops, and non-UTF-8, empty and all-`(` input are all safe.
- The string rule matches ruststep exactly: `string` is `'` { `''` | none_of(`'`) } `'`, with no backslash escapes. The comment rule also matches: `/*` ... `*/` with no nesting, and `/*/` does not close the comment. A quote inside a comment, or `/*` inside a string, is handled the same way on both sides.
- Every entry point is guarded. In `crates/app`, outside `crates/kernel`, only `step::parse_with_chord` and `step_csys::read_tool_csys` call `ruststep::parser::parse`. `step_units` only walks an AST that has already been parsed, and `tool_body.rs` / `tool_body_view.rs` reach ruststep through `read_tool_csys`. The HEADER is scanned too, because the scan covers every byte.
- The message names the cap, the entity and the line, and counting `\n` gives the same line for LF and CRLF. The new module has its provenance comment, both files are under 400 lines, the decision file is present, the `Changelog:` line is present and the tests run in the default lane.

### Local results (trial merge with main a6bd69d8, already up to date)
| run | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test step_nesting` | 5/5 pass |
| `--test import` | 23/23 pass |
| `--test tool_csys` | 11/11 pass |
| `--test step_chord_units` | 3/3 pass |
| `--test model_fidelity` | 9/9 pass |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib step` | 17/17 pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_depth.rs:100-130`: `<...>` spans are not skipped, so the scan can be fooled.**
   - In ruststep, `resource` (REFERENCE section, `#n = <...>;`) and `anchor_name` (ANCHOR section) are `'<' none_of('>')* '>'` (`ruststep/src/parser/token.rs:86-90` and `:187-191` at rev 90fdc93). Inside one, `'`, `/*` and `(` are plain characters.
   - The scan reads them as a string opener or a comment opener and stays in that state past the `>`. Every parenthesis after it is skipped, but ruststep goes on to parse the DATA section normally.
   - Reproduction (throwaway probe, not committed): take box.step and insert this before `DATA;`
     ```
     REFERENCE;
     #900000 = <x/*y>;
     ENDSEC;
     ```
     then add a record nested 5000 deep before the DATA `ENDSEC;`. The result:
     ```
     check ok = true
     thread 'probe_crash_5000' has overflowed its stack
     process didn't exit successfully: ... (exit code: 0xc00000fd, STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW)
     ```
     The same input with depth 100: the scan reports a max depth of 3, `ruststep::parser::parse` returns Ok, and `import::parse_model` returns Ok. The `'` opener (`<x'y>`) gives the same result.
   - Fix: add a `State::Uri` that the `Code` state enters on `<` and leaves on `>`, skipping everything in between, exactly as ruststep does (ruststep reads `<` only as the start of a resource or anchor name). The same change stops valid URIs that contain `(` or `'` from being refused wrongly.
   - Pin it with a test for both openers, `<x/*y>` and `<x'y>`, in a REFERENCE section followed by a record at depth 65, which must be refused. Keep the depth at 65 so no test can overflow the stack.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- **Cap margin.** 64 against a measured 400 (debug, 1 MiB) is about 6x, and the guard runs before any parse frames exist, so the margin is convincing. The workspace has no `stack_size` call outside `crates/kernel`, so the import threads get Rust's 2 MiB default or the 1 MiB Windows main thread. No thread smaller than 1 MiB was found.
- **Recursion is driven only by parentheses.** ruststep recurses through `list`, `typed_parameter` and `anchor_item_list`, and all three open with `(`. References are not followed at parse time. Binary `"..."` literals are not supported by ruststep (`// FIXME binary`), so a `(` inside one can only be over-counted, never under-counted.
- **PR #1006.** Merging `refs/pull/1006/head` on top of this PR merges `step.rs` cleanly, but `crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs` conflicts: both PRs add a `pub mod` line in the same place. Keep both lines; it is a trivial conflict.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 45472061461e630ae50d67501a2e1f374e390d2c -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The blocker from the last review (deep records hidden behind `<...>`) is fixed. A second attempt to get a deep record past the scan found no way through.

### What looks good
- The new `Uri` state matches ruststep at rev 90fdc93. `resource` (`token.rs:86-90`) and `anchor_name` (`token.rs:187-191`) are both `<`, then anything but `>`, then `>`. I checked the tokenizer directly rather than relying on the PR's table.
- Only four ruststep parsers consume free text: strings, comments, `<...>` resources and anchor names. No other `none_of`, `anychar`, `take_*` or `satisfy` parser consumes `'`, `<` or `/*`, so the scan has exactly the right set of skip states.
- `"` (binary) is a parse error in ruststep, and the scan still counts `(` inside it, so it can only over-count.
- ruststep recurses only through `list`, `typed_parameter`, `subsuper_record` and `anchor_item_list`, and all of them open with `(`.
- The new `Cargo.toml` note asks for a re-audit when the pin moves.

### Attack probes (throwaway test file, not committed)
**Records nested 65 deep that the scan must refuse.** All 24 of these constructs were refused:
- plain lists, `T(` typed nests, mixed `T((`
- a complex entity `(A(...)B(1))`
- `'x'''`, `'x\'`, and `\X2\`/`\S\` text
- `/` then a newline then `*`
- a `'` or `<` inside a comment
- `<a'b>` and `<a/*b>` in REFERENCE, and `<a'b>` as an ANCHOR name
- a deep ANCHOR item, and a deep ANCHOR tag `{t:(...)}`
- deep `DATA(...)` parameters, a second DATA section, and a deep record in the HEADER
- a lowercase keyword, `ENDSEC; DATA;` inside a string
- a UTF-8 BOM, a NUL byte, a `!USR` keyword and an `@999=` instance

**The one case where the scan loses sync** is `<a'>'b>` in REFERENCE. ruststep closes the resource at the first `>` and fails on the next `'`. `opt_(reference_section)` then backtracks, and the parse stops with an error, so the DATA section is never reached. I confirmed this in a separate process with a record 2000 deep: the import returns `syntax error ... at line 7` and does not overflow. The underlying rule is that ruststep stops at its first syntax error, so a loss of sync after that point is harmless.

**Valid files are not refused.** All nine `testdata/models/*.step` files are at depth 3 and pass. A file whose string holds 500 `(` and whose REFERENCE holds `<http://x/a(b)(c'd>` imports.

**No hang or panic.**
- Unterminated nests 64 deep (typed, list, complex) fail cleanly in about 2 ms each, so backtracking does not blow up.
- Empty input, and a lone `(`, `'`, `<`, `"`, `/*`, `/` or `#` with a 25-digit id, are handled without a panic, as are `0xff` bytes.
- A file of 10 M `(` is refused in microseconds.

### Local results (trial merge with main, already up to date)
| run | result |
|---|---|
| `--test step_nesting` | 8/8 pass |
| `--test import` | 23/23 pass |
| `--test tool_csys` | 11/11 pass |
| `--test step_chord_units` | 3/3 pass |
| `--test model_fidelity` | 9/9 pass |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib step` | 18/18 pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- `step_depth.rs` is 250 lines. `crates/app/tests/step_nesting.rs` is 335 lines, under the limit.
- PR #1006 still conflicts with this PR only in `import/mod.rs`, where both add a `pub mod` line. Keep both lines.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
